name: Creaky Floorboards
tagline: Two retired ladies. One microphone. Zero correct answers (until week four).
notes: Plays automatically on the radio every morning (weeks 1-4) while the player explores; nobody can be talked to until it ends, so keep each episode to roughly 120-180 words. ep5 plays after the final inspection, only if the whole house passed (housefixed). Lukey's mystery is the main story (ep4 is his reveal); each episode also teases one of the others with a hint, never a statement: Tyler (the saluting man in a navy blazer, ep1), Wyatt (the porch light and 'a certain year', ep2; the missing January 2000 paper, ep4), Malcolm (poetry in a closet, ep3). Lines are 'Speaker: text'; *...* lines are sound cues.

ep1.title: Episode 1: The Catfish of Heartbreak Lane
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Bev: Welcome back to Creaky Floorboards! I'm Bev.
Trish: And I'm Trish. We solve the mysteries the police were too busy to care about.
Bev: This week: 12 Heartbreak Lane. Condemned. Damp. And some young flipper's just bought it.
Trish: Neighbors report dripping. At night. Inside the walls.
Bev: My theory? A catfish. Enormous. Lives in the walls, eats the drywall.
Trish: Bev, I think SHE'S being catfished. Who's texting her at two in the morning?
Bev: THE CATFISH, Trish.
Trish: Listener mail. 'I saw a young man in a navy blazer saluting me from the bathroom window. I looked again and nobody was there.'
Bev: Military catfish. Did you salute back?
Trish: She did not.
Trish: ...Stay creaky.

ep2.title: Episode 2: Something in the Walls Is Singing
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Trish: Update, listeners. We interviewed the next-door neighbor, Mrs. Pruitt.
Bev: Lovely woman. Eighty-two. Nine cats. One crossbow.
Mrs. Pruitt: Somebody's singing Bon Jovi in the walls of number twelve. Very flat. Very confident.
Bev: Classic catfish.
Trish: Catfish don't sing, Bev.
Bev: Not with THAT attitude.
Mrs. Pruitt: And their porch light comes on for me every night. Nobody touches the switch. I wave. It flickers back.
Mrs. Pruitt: Sometimes it hums along. Something about partying like it's a certain year. It dips at the year.
Trish: That sounds electrical, Bev.
Bev: Electric catfish.
Trish: That's an eel. Next week, a very special guest. Stay creaky!

ep3.title: Episode 3: The Inspector
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Trish: This week, an exclusive. City building inspector Dan has agreed to talk to us.
Dan: Happy to be here, ladies. Big fan. I listen while I inspect. It's very soothing.
Bev: Dan. 12 Heartbreak Lane. Haunted? Yes or no.
Dan: The only thing haunting that house is its water pressure.
Trish: Is it true you asked the new owner out for coffee?
Dan: To discuss PERMITS. ...And then my shoes filled up with water. Both of them. On a dry day.
Bev: That's the catfish, Dan.
Trish: A listener says she heard a man in a closet at number twelve reciting poetry. Forty pages. About a banana.
Dan: That's just the mold, ladies. A fungus among us! A real moldy oldie!
*Nobody laughs. Dan laughs for some time.*
Trish: And a weather bulletin: BIG STORM SATURDAY. Heavy rain, flooding and power cuts across the county.
Bev: Next week: the library. Stay creaky!

ep4.title: Episode 4: We Went to the Library
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo. Then, unusually, silence.*
Bev: Listeners. We went to the library.
Trish: We touched MICROFICHE, Bev.
Bev: And Trish found it. The local paper, 1987.
Trish: 'Local aerobics instructor Luke Moretti, 34, died in 1987 when a cast-iron pipe fell on his head as he attempted to repair a woman's sink before their first date.'
Bev: BEFORE the date. He never even got the DATE, Trish.
Trish: The woman was a Brenda. It was her house. 12 Heartbreak Lane.
Bev: A man died trying to impress a woman with his DIY. That's every man I've ever dated.
Trish: Most of them lived, Bev.
Bev: ...So no catfish?
Trish: No catfish. Odd thing, though: the January 2nd, 2000 paper is missing. The librarian said it's 'probably in somebody's wall.'
Bev: Librarians are very dark, Trish.
Trish: The storm's here, listeners. Batten down. Stay creaky.

ep5.title: Episode 5: Case Closed (Mostly)
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, a kazoo and, this week, a celebratory gong.*
Trish: We're LIVE from the front porch of 12 Heartbreak Lane. It passed inspection. Case closed.
Bev: Mostly closed. I still think there's a catfish.
Trish: Every leak, fixed. The mold, gone. The wiring, redone. And the pink bathroom, restored. Dan called it a keeper.
Bev: We asked the owner about Luke Moretti. And the man in the blazer. And the poetry in the closet. And the porch light.
Trish: She said, and I quote, 'It's complicated.'
Bev: Which is the most romantic thing anyone's ever said about home repair.
Trish: Dan says his shoes have been dry for a whole week, and he's never been so sad. Final thoughts, Bev?
Bev: Never trust a man who says he's great with his hands.
*SPLASH. A bucket of water tips off the porch railing and soaks Bev completely.*
Trish: ...Stay creaky, everybody.
